label: Facing foreclosure
h1: Stop Foreclosure in North Carolina by Selling Your House
metaTitle: Stop Foreclosure in NC | Sell Your House Before the Sale Date
metaDescription: Behind on payments in Gaston or Cleveland County? You can sell a house in foreclosure in NC right up to the sale, and often during the 10-day upset bid period after it. Written cash offer in 24 hours.
directAnswer: Yes, you can sell your house during foreclosure in North Carolina. Until the property is sold at auction and the 10-day upset bid period closes, you still own the house and can sell it. The sale pays off the lender, stops the foreclosure, and any equity above what you owe goes to you instead of being lost at auction.
painPoints: You have a Notice of Hearing from the Clerk of Superior Court and a date on the calendar.
You owe more in arrears than you can catch up in one payment.
An agent told you there isn't time to list it.
You have equity in the house and you are about to lose all of it at auction.
The phone calls and the certified letters have not stopped.

processSteps.title: Tell us the sale date first
processSteps.body: It is the only fact that sets the schedule. If there is a date, everything below compresses to fit it.

processSteps.title: We get the payoff, not an estimate
processSteps.body: With your written authorization we contact the servicer or the trustee's attorney directly for the actual reinstatement and payoff figures. Most sellers are working from numbers that are weeks out of date.

processSteps.title: Written offer within 24 hours
processSteps.body: You see exactly what you walk away with after the loan is satisfied. If that number is worse than letting it go to auction, we will tell you.

processSteps.title: We close through a North Carolina closing attorney
processSteps.body: The attorney pays the lender directly from closing funds, the foreclosure is cancelled, and the balance comes to you.

faq.q: Can I still sell my house if foreclosure has already started in NC?
faq.a: Yes. In North Carolina you own the house and can sell it up until the foreclosure sale is final. Even after the auction, North Carolina has a 10-day upset bid period during which the sale is not yet final, and payoff is sometimes still possible. The closer you are to the date, the fewer options you have, so the sale date is the first thing to tell us.

faq.q: What happens to my equity if the house sells at auction?
faq.a: Foreclosure auctions routinely bring less than market value. The lender is paid first, along with fees and costs. Whatever is left is supposed to come to you, but it is frequently very little or nothing. Selling before the auction is how you protect equity you have actually built.

faq.q: Will selling to a cash buyer hurt my credit less than foreclosure?
faq.a: A completed foreclosure stays on your credit report for seven years and is one of the most damaging entries there is. A sale that pays the loan in full is reported as a satisfied loan. We are not credit counselors and you should confirm specifics with one, but the difference is significant.

faq.q: How fast can you actually close if my sale date is soon?
faq.a: Our normal close is 7 to 21 days. When there is a foreclosure date we work to it. What determines the floor is title work and the attorney's schedule, not our funding. Tell us the date on the first call and we will tell you honestly whether we can make it.

faq.q: Do I have to pay anything to sell this way?
faq.a: No. There is no commission, no fee to us, and we pay the standard closing costs. If the payoff exceeds what the house is worth, we will tell you that too rather than waste your time.

label: Inherited a house
h1: Sell an Inherited House in North Carolina Without Repairing It First
metaTitle: Sell an Inherited House in NC | Probate-Friendly Cash Buyer
metaDescription: Inherited a house in Gaston or Cleveland County? We buy inherited and probate properties as-is, cleanout included, and coordinate with the estate attorney. Written offer in 24 hours.
directAnswer: In North Carolina, real property generally passes to the heirs or devisees at the moment of death, which means heirs can often sell an inherited house without waiting for the full estate to close. Whether the personal representative needs to be involved depends on the will and on whether the estate has debts, so the estate attorney is the one to confirm it for your situation.
painPoints: The house is three hours away and you cannot keep driving out to check on it.
It is full, and clearing it out means deciding what to do with a lifetime of belongings.
You and your siblings do not agree on what to do.
Insurance on a vacant house is expensive and getting harder to keep.
Taxes, utilities, and lawn care are coming out of your pocket every month.

processSteps.title: Tell us where the estate stands
processSteps.body: Has an executor or administrator been appointed by the Clerk of Superior Court? Is there a will? How many heirs? This determines who has to sign, and it is worth getting right at the start.

processSteps.title: We walk it once, as-is
processSteps.body: Leave it exactly as it is. Do not clean it out, do not haul anything, do not fix anything. We have seen worse than what is in there.

processSteps.title: Written offer within 24 hours, sent to every heir
processSteps.body: One number, in writing, that every sibling can read at the same time. This alone resolves a surprising number of family disagreements.

processSteps.title: We work on the estate's timeline
processSteps.body: If the estate needs more time before it can convey, we wait. We will not pressure a family into closing before the clerk's office is ready.

faq.q: Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished in North Carolina?
faq.a: Often yes. In North Carolina real property generally vests in the heirs or devisees at death, so the heirs may be able to convey it directly. It gets more complicated if the estate has debts that require the personal representative to sell the property to create assets. Your estate attorney should confirm which applies before you sign anything, and we are happy to work directly with them.

faq.q: What if my siblings and I do not agree?
faq.a: Every heir who holds an interest has to sign the deed. We cannot buy without all of them. What we can do is put one written number in front of everyone at once, which is usually more productive than each person estimating what the house is worth.

faq.q: Do we have to clean the house out first?
faq.a: No. Take what matters to you and leave everything else. Cleanout is our cost, not yours, and it is included in the offer rather than deducted from it.

faq.q: Will we owe taxes on the sale?
faq.a: Inherited property generally receives a stepped-up basis to its value at the date of death, which often means little or no capital gain if you sell near that value. That is a general statement and not tax advice. Talk to a CPA about your specific situation before you close.

faq.q: What if the house has a reverse mortgage or a lien on it?
faq.a: Both are common on inherited houses and neither is a dealbreaker. Reverse mortgages have a payoff deadline after the borrower's death, which usually makes speed more valuable, not less. The closing attorney will identify every lien in the title search and they are paid at closing.

label: Going through a divorce
h1: Sell a House During Divorce in North Carolina
metaTitle: Sell Your House Fast During Divorce | Gaston & Cleveland County NC
metaDescription: Selling a marital home in a North Carolina divorce. One written offer both parties can see, a clean date, and no months of showings. Gaston and Cleveland County.
directAnswer: A marital home in North Carolina is typically sold either by agreement between the parties or under a court order as part of equitable distribution. Both spouses on the deed generally have to sign. A cash sale gives both sides a single written number and a fixed closing date, which removes the recurring argument about price reductions and showings.
painPoints: Neither of you can afford the mortgage alone.
One of you has moved out and is paying for two places.
You cannot agree on a list price, and every price reduction reopens the argument.
Showings mean coordinating with someone you are actively separating from.
Your attorneys are billing hourly while the house sits.

processSteps.title: We work with both parties or with the attorneys
processSteps.body: Whichever is less painful. If communication is going through counsel, we will communicate through counsel.

processSteps.title: One written offer, sent to both sides simultaneously
processSteps.body: Same document, same time, no one hearing it secondhand.

processSteps.title: You pick the date
processSteps.body: If the closing needs to line up with a separation agreement or a court date, we work to it.

processSteps.title: Proceeds split at closing per your agreement
processSteps.body: The closing attorney disburses according to whatever you and your counsel have agreed or the court has ordered.

faq.q: Do both spouses have to agree to sell?
faq.a: Generally both parties on the deed must sign to convey. In North Carolina, a spouse may also have marital interest considerations even if not on the deed. Your family law attorney is the right person to confirm what applies to you, and we will not proceed without the signatures the closing attorney requires.

faq.q: Can we sell before the divorce is final?
faq.a: Frequently yes, by agreement. Many couples sell during separation specifically so the proceeds can be divided cleanly. Your attorney should review any agreement before you sign it.

faq.q: What if one of us wants to keep the house?
faq.a: Then do not sell it to us. If one party can refinance into their own name and buy the other out, that is usually the better outcome, and we will say so.

faq.q: How is this different from listing with an agent?
faq.a: A listing means agreeing on price, agreeing on every reduction, keeping the house presentable, and coordinating showings, all with someone you are separating from, for however long it takes. A cash sale is one number and one date.

label: Done being a landlord
h1: Sell a Rental Property in North Carolina, Tenants and All
metaTitle: Sell Your Rental Property Fast | Tenant-Occupied OK | Gaston & Cleveland County NC
metaDescription: Sell a tenant-occupied or vacant rental in Gaston or Cleveland County without turning it over first. We buy with tenants in place, damage and all. Written offer in 24 hours.
directAnswer: You can sell a tenant-occupied rental in North Carolina without ending the lease. The buyer takes the property subject to the existing lease, which transfers with the sale. This means you do not have to evict, turn the unit, or wait for a vacancy to sell.
painPoints: The tenant has stopped paying and you do not want to run an eviction.
The unit needs a full turn before it could ever be listed.
You inherited the property and never wanted to be a landlord.
You are managing it from another state.
The repair list has grown faster than the rent.

processSteps.title: Send the rent roll and the lease
processSteps.body: Current rent, lease end date, deposit held, payment history. That plus the address is usually enough for a first number.

processSteps.title: We can buy with the tenant in place
processSteps.body: No eviction, no turn, no notice to vacate. The lease transfers with the property.

processSteps.title: One interior walk, scheduled around the tenant
processSteps.body: We give proper notice and we are not going to make their life difficult.

processSteps.title: Close and stop paying for it
processSteps.body: Deposits and prorated rent are handled at closing by the attorney.

faq.q: Can I sell with a tenant still living there?
faq.a: Yes. In North Carolina a lease generally survives the sale, and the buyer takes subject to it. We buy tenant-occupied properties regularly and do not require you to deliver the property vacant.

faq.q: What if the tenant has not paid in months?
faq.a: That is our problem after closing, not a reason for us to walk. It does affect the number, because it affects what we are buying, but it does not stop the sale.

faq.q: What about the security deposit?
faq.a: North Carolina has specific requirements for how deposits are held and transferred. The closing attorney handles the transfer or credit at closing so that it is documented properly.

faq.q: Do you buy small portfolios?
faq.a: Yes. If you have several properties you want out of at once, tell us on the first call. It is usually simpler for everyone to handle them together.

label: House needs major repairs
h1: Sell a House That Needs Major Repairs in North Carolina
metaTitle: Sell a House As-Is That Needs Repairs | Gaston & Cleveland County NC
metaDescription: Foundation, roof, fire or water damage, mold, failed septic. We buy houses in Gaston and Cleveland County in any condition, as-is, with no repairs and no repair renegotiation after you sign.
directAnswer: A house with major structural, roof, electrical, or water damage often cannot be financed by a retail buyer, because most conventional and FHA lenders will not lend against a property in that condition. That is why these houses sell for cash. We buy as-is, we walk it before we price it, and we do not come back afterward asking for a repair credit.
painPoints: The roof is at the end of its life and insurance has already been out.
There is foundation movement, and every buyer's inspector will find it.
There was a fire or a burst pipe and the repairs stalled.
There is mold, and the estimate to remediate is more than you can fund.
An agent told you it has to be listed as-is, cash only.

processSteps.title: Send photos, or do not
processSteps.body: Whatever is easiest. We are going to walk it either way and we are not going to be surprised.

processSteps.title: One walkthrough, no inspector, no contractor parade
processSteps.body: You will not have half a dozen people tramping through giving estimates.

processSteps.title: Written offer within 24 hours, as-is
processSteps.body: The condition is priced in. There is no repair addendum coming after the fact.

processSteps.title: We don't re-trade you on condition
processSteps.body: The number we put in writing is the number at closing. There is no repair addendum and no inspection deduction coming after the fact. This is the most common complaint about cash buyers and we do not do it.

faq.q: Do I need to fix anything before you will buy?
faq.a: No. Not the roof, not the HVAC, not the floors. If we wanted a renovated house we would buy a renovated house.

faq.q: What if there is mold or asbestos?
faq.a: Both are common in pre-1980 housing, which is most of what we buy in Gaston and Cleveland County. Neither stops a sale. They do affect the number, because they affect our cost to make the house habitable.

faq.q: The house was in a fire. Will you still buy it?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us whether an insurance claim has been paid out and whether the carrier has already settled, because that affects who owns what at closing.

faq.q: Can I sell if the house has been condemned or has code violations?
faq.a: Usually yes. Open code enforcement cases and municipal liens are found in the title search and resolved at closing. Tell us about them up front so there are no surprises that delay the date.

label: Relocating or job transfer
h1: Sell Your House Fast When You Are Relocating
metaTitle: Relocating? Sell Your House Fast in Gaston & Cleveland County NC
metaDescription: Job transfer, military orders, or a move on a deadline. Pick your closing date and sell without carrying two housing payments. Written cash offer in 24 hours.
directAnswer: The problem with relocating is not price, it is certainty. A listing can fall through at the appraisal or the buyer's financing two weeks before you have to be in another state. A cash sale with no financing contingency removes that risk and lets you pick the closing date to match your move.
painPoints: You have a start date and the house is not sold.
You are about to pay a mortgage here and rent somewhere else.
A listing fell through at financing and you are back to zero.
You have military orders with a hard report date.
You cannot manage showings from another state.

processSteps.title: Tell us your date
processSteps.body: We build the closing around it rather than the other way around.

processSteps.title: Written offer within 24 hours
processSteps.body: You can make the rest of your decisions knowing the number.

processSteps.title: Close before you go, or after
processSteps.body: North Carolina closings can generally be handled remotely with the attorney's coordination if you have already moved.

processSteps.title: Leave what you do not want to move
processSteps.body: Furniture, appliances, the contents of the garage. Moving less is cheaper.

faq.q: Can I close after I have already moved out of state?
faq.a: Generally yes. North Carolina requires an attorney-supervised closing, and the attorney can usually coordinate signing remotely. Confirm the specifics with the closing attorney early so there are no surprises.

faq.q: What if my company is paying for relocation?
faq.a: Many relocation packages include a guaranteed buyout, and if yours does, compare it to our offer carefully. Sometimes theirs is better. We will tell you if it looks that way.

faq.q: Can I stay in the house after closing?
faq.a: Often yes, with a short post-closing occupancy agreement. Tell us how long you need and we will put it in writing rather than leave it as a handshake.

faq.q: How is this better than just listing it?
faq.a: If you have three or four months and the house shows well, listing it will probably net you more, and we will say so. If you have three weeks and a hard date, certainty is worth more than the last few percent.

label: Vacant or unwanted house
h1: Sell a Vacant House in Gaston or Cleveland County
metaTitle: Sell a Vacant House Fast in NC | No Repairs, No Cleanout
metaDescription: A vacant house costs you every month in taxes, insurance, and risk. We buy vacant and neglected houses in Gaston and Cleveland County as-is. Written offer in 24 hours.
directAnswer: A vacant house is expensive to hold. Most standard homeowner policies restrict or void coverage once a property has been vacant for 30 to 60 days, and vacant-property insurance costs considerably more. Meanwhile taxes, utilities, and lawn maintenance continue, and vacancy itself accelerates deterioration through copper theft, vandalism, and undetected water damage.
painPoints: Your insurer has flagged it as vacant or is refusing to renew.
You are paying taxes and utilities on a house nobody lives in.
The city has sent letters about the grass or the condition.
Something has already been stolen or broken into.
You have been meaning to deal with it for two years.

processSteps.title: Tell us how long it has been empty
processSteps.body: It matters for what we will find inside, and we would rather know than be surprised.

processSteps.title: We will meet you there, or use a lockbox
processSteps.body: If you are out of the area, you do not have to drive out.

processSteps.title: Written offer within 24 hours, contents included
processSteps.body: Whatever is still in there stays. Cleanout is our cost.

processSteps.title: Stop paying for it
processSteps.body: Taxes and insurance prorate at closing and the carrying cost ends.

faq.q: The house has been empty for years. Will you still buy it?
faq.a: Yes. Long-vacant houses are a large share of what we buy. Expect the number to reflect condition, because years of vacancy usually mean water damage, and water damage is the expensive kind.

faq.q: There is still furniture and belongings inside. Do I have to clear it?
faq.a: No. Take what you want and leave the rest. Cleanout is included in the offer, not deducted from it.

faq.q: What if I owe back property taxes?
faq.a: Delinquent taxes are a lien and are paid from the proceeds at closing. As long as the sale price covers the liens, back taxes do not stop a sale. If they exceed the value, tell us early and we will be straight with you about it.

faq.q: What if I do not have the deed or cannot find the paperwork?
faq.a: That is normal and rarely a problem. The closing attorney searches title at the Register of Deeds and establishes the chain of ownership. Missing paperwork on your end is not usually the obstacle people expect it to be.

label: Pet damage or hoarding
h1: Sell a House With Pet Damage or Hoarding Conditions in North Carolina
metaTitle: Sell a House With Pet Damage in NC | Cat Urine, Odor, Hoarding | No Cleanup
metaDescription: Cat urine, pet odor, or a house that's been let go. We buy in Gaston and Cleveland County as-is, with no cleanup and no judgment. Written cash offer in 24 hours.
directAnswer: A house with heavy pet urine damage often cannot be financed by a retail buyer. FHA appraisers are required to assess whether a property is free of hazards, odors and physical defects, and VA appraisals require a property to be safe, structurally sound and sanitary. A house that smells strongly of cat urine gets flagged, the loan stalls, and the buyer pool collapses to cash. That is why these houses sell to cash buyers, and it is not a reflection on you.
painPoints: The smell has gotten into the floors and you can't get it out.
You're embarrassed to let an agent walk through it.
A relative's house was let go further than anyone outside the family knew.
You've been quoted more to clean and repair it than you think it's worth.
You've already had a buyer walk after they opened the front door.

processSteps.title: You don't have to clean anything first
processSteps.body: Not the carpet, not the litter boxes, not the rooms you've been keeping shut. We have walked houses in worse shape than yours and we are not going to react.

processSteps.title: We look at what's underneath, not what's on top
processSteps.body: With pet damage the question is always how far down it went: carpet and pad, then subfloor, then framing. That's what sets the number, and we can usually tell within twenty minutes.

processSteps.title: Written offer within 24 hours, cleanout included
processSteps.body: Whatever is in the house stays. Furniture, belongings, anything you don't want to sort through. Clearing it is our cost, not a deduction from your offer.

processSteps.title: Nobody else walks through
processSteps.body: No showings, no open house, no parade of strangers reacting to the smell of your family member's home. One walkthrough with us and that's the last one.

faq.q: Why can't I just clean it and list it?
faq.a: Sometimes you can, and if that's the right answer we'll say so. The problem with cat urine specifically is that the uric acid forms crystals that don't dissolve in water, so mopping and carpet cleaning don't remove them. They sit in the subfloor and reactivate with humidity, which is why a house can smell fine in February and awful in July. Proper remediation usually means pulling the flooring, treating and sealing the subfloor with a shellac-based stain-blocking primer, and often replacing boards where it soaked through. It is real work, not a deep clean.

faq.q: Will pet odor really stop someone getting a mortgage?
faq.a: It can. FHA appraisal standards require the appraiser to consider whether the property is free of hazards, odors and physical defects, and VA appraisals require a property to be safe, structurally sound and sanitary. A strong odor is exactly the kind of thing that gets called out, and once it is in the appraisal the lender wants it fixed before they will fund. That is the mechanism that pushes these houses to cash.

faq.q: How much does pet damage take off the offer?
faq.a: It depends entirely on depth. Surface-level odor in a house with tile floors is close to nothing, because tile doesn't absorb. Urine that has gone through carpet, through pad, into subfloor and up the bottom of the drywall is a floor replacement plus sealing plus trim and doors, and that is a real number. We'll show you the arithmetic rather than just handing you a lower figure.

faq.q: The house was a hoarding situation. Is that different?
faq.a: Same answer: leave it. Take out what matters to your family and we handle the rest. Hoarding and pet situations usually travel together and we treat both the same way, without commentary. You are not the first person to call us about this and you will not be the last.

faq.q: Do I have to tell buyers about it if I clean it up myself?
faq.a: North Carolina has disclosure obligations for sellers, and a material defect you know about does not stop being material because you painted over it. This is a question for a North Carolina real estate attorney, not for us. What we can tell you is that when you sell to us as-is, the condition is already priced in and there is nothing to disclose around.
